bug: Closing a checkpoint store did not settle callers waiting for its database open. A blocked request could leave single or concurrent loads pending indefinitely after disposal.

before.observations: After close and eight microtask turns, neither the one-load nor three-load fixture had settled any callers. Releasing the held native success event allowed cleanup.

fix: Settle the owner's shared pending open on explicit close, without claiming to cancel the platform request.
Retain terminal handlers to abort late upgrades and close late connections, including closure during schema validation.
Suppress closed-owner blocked-progress notifications and release the cancellation closure after open settlement.
Preserve transaction completion semantics for writes already dispatched.

verification.typecheck: passed (runtime, unit tests and browser tests)

scenarios: Real database deletion blocked by a retained connection; two loads queued behind it settle on owner close before unblock; late upgrade aborts with AbortError.
Normal checkpoint save, real page reload, Undo and Redo.

limits: The browser probe creates and deletes only its own database in a fresh isolated test context.
Native open requests cannot be canceled. Native resource cleanup still waits for a platform event; only owner-side open waiters are settled immediately.
Pending digest operations and already-dispatched transaction behavior are unchanged; no write timeout was introduced.
The separate WebKit numeric fault remains unresolved; native instrumentation stayed paused.
No full release qualification, commit, push or publication is claimed.
